cleanIntro: ⛔ Two rules govern this rifle and both are McMillan's own words: never fire it without the muzzle brake, and never put WD-40 on any part of it. Beyond that the routine is a bolt gun's — bolt out on the bolt stop release, bore cleaned from the CHAMBER end with a bronze brush and a bore guide, and the muzzle held LOWER than the action so the solvent runs out of the barrel instead of down into the trigger. Clean at 30 to 40 rounds if you want the accuracy this rifle was bought for.

steps.title: Safety to the REAR, bolt up and back, then empty the chamber and magazine
steps.action: Point it somewhere safe and move the safety lever to the rear — that is the SAFE position on this rifle, and McMillan add the instruction to keep your finger off the trigger WHILE you move it. Raise the bolt handle, pull the bolt all the way back and take any ammunition out of the chamber and the magazine.
steps.quote: Avoid touching the trigger while moving the safety lever.
steps.cite: McMillan TAC-50 Series Owner's Manual — McMillan-TAC-50-Series-Owners-Manual (the file McMillan publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — REMOVAL OF THE BOLT ASSEMBLY

steps.title: Bolt out on the bolt stop release — the buttstock may have to come off first
steps.action: With the bolt fully rearward, depress the bolt stop release and slide the bolt out as you hold it depressed. On some configurations there is not enough room behind the action and the buttstock has to come off to give clearance; McMillan say so rather than leaving you levering at it.
steps.aside: rifle. The butt stock may have to be removed for clearance.

steps.title: Look down the bore from the CHAMBER end, every time
steps.action: Bolt out, look through the barrel from the chamber end to the muzzle. This is the one inspection that has to happen before the rifle is fired again. ⛔ And if something is in there that a cleaning rod will not push out, the rifle goes back to McMillan — never try to clear it by firing another round.
steps.caution:
NEVER try to remove an object from the barrel by loading another 
cartridge and firing.
steps.quote: Look through the barrel from the chamber end to the muzzle.
steps.cite: McMillan TAC-50 Series Owner's Manual — McMillan-TAC-50-Series-Owners-Manual (the file McMillan publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — BARREL INSPECTION PROCEDURE

steps.title: Muzzle LOWER than the action, and clean at 30 to 40 rounds
steps.action: Take out the magazine, buttstock and bolt, and set the rifle so the MUZZLE SITS LOWER THAN THE ACTION before you start pushing solvent through. That is not fussiness — it is what keeps solvent running out of the muzzle instead of down into the action and the trigger. McMillan's interval for benchrest accuracy with moly or copper-jacketed bullets is 30 to 40 rounds.
steps.aside:
Clean the rifle after 30 to 40 rounds in order to maintain 
“benchrest accuracy.”
steps.quote: Ensure the muzzle is lower than the action.
steps.cite: McMillan TAC-50 Series Owner's Manual — McMillan-TAC-50-Series-Owners-Manual (the file McMillan publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — CLEANING PROCEDURE

steps.title: Bronze brush from the chamber end — never stainless
steps.action: Always clean from the chamber towards the muzzle, with a bore guide in place, a coated rod and a good bronze brush. ⛔ Never a stainless brush: McMillan state it damages the bore, and on a barrel of this cost that is an expensive five minutes.
steps.aside:
Always clean the barrel from the chamber end towards the 
muzzle.
steps.quote:
We recommend a 
good quality bronze brush (never use stainless steel brushes as 
they can damage the bore), coated cleaning rod, bore guide, brass 
jag, and soft clean patches.
steps.cite: McMillan TAC-50 Series Owner's Manual — McMillan-TAC-50-Series-Owners-Manual (the file McMillan publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — NEW RIFLE BREAK-IN PROCEDURES

steps.title: Bolt: solvent on the body, brush the face, then LIFT the extractor
steps.action: Wipe the bolt body down with solvent and a rag until the fouling is gone, then take a bristle brush to the bolt face and clear the loose brass off it. The step people skip is the next one — lift the extractor and clean UNDER the extractor notch, which is where the brass shavings actually collect.
steps.quote:
Lift the extractor upward and clean under the extractor notch
with the brush and solvent.
steps.cite: McMillan TAC-50 Series Owner's Manual — McMillan-TAC-50-Series-Owners-Manual (the file McMillan publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — CLEANING THE BOLT ASSEMBLY

steps.title: Work the ejector and extractor — a sticky one goes back to McMillan
steps.action: After the bolt is dry and lightly oiled, activate the ejector and the extractor and make sure both move freely without sticking. McMillan's instruction if either sticks is not to free it up yourself: return the rifle. Then a LIGHT film of grease behind the bolt locking lugs — light, because over-greasing there is the usual mistake.
steps.caution:
If the ejector or the extractor sticks, return the rifle
to McMillan.
steps.quote:
Activate the ejector and the extractor and ensure they move
freely without sticking.
steps.cite: McMillan TAC-50 Series Owner's Manual — McMillan-TAC-50-Series-Owners-Manual (the file McMillan publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — CLEANING THE BOLT ASSEMBLY

steps.title: ⛔ Never WD-40, and go easy on the bore oil
steps.action: For storage the rifle is cleaned and thoroughly oiled, with only a very light film in the bore — over-oil it and the oil works its way down into the action. ⛔ And not WD-40, anywhere: McMillan name it, because it is a water-displacing oil that dries out and leaves a sticky varnish behind on precisely the surfaces you need to move.
steps.aside:
The bore should be coated with a very light layer of oil. Avoid over oiling the bore as it will work 
its way down into the acton.
steps.quote:
NEVER use WD-40 on any part of the rifle. WD-40 is a water 
displacing oil and will dry out, leaving a sticky varnish behind.
steps.cite: McMillan TAC-50 Series Owner's Manual — McMillan-TAC-50-Series-Owners-Manual (the file McMillan publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — Lubrication

steps.title: Receiver and trigger cleaned AS A UNIT, out of the stock
steps.action: Safety to the rear, bolt out, rifle upside down, and take out the two action screws so the stock lifts away. Then clean the receiver and trigger assembly TOGETHER as one unit with a degreaser — and get the degreaser off coated surfaces as soon as you are done, rather than letting it sit.
steps.quote:
Clean the receiver and trigger assembly as a unit with a 
degreaser. Do not leave any degreaser on coated surfaces any longer
than necessary.
steps.cite: McMillan TAC-50 Series Owner's Manual — McMillan-TAC-50-Series-Owners-Manual (the file McMillan publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — CLEANING THE RECEIVER AND TRIGGER ASSEMBLY

steps.title: Bolt lugs at 12 and 6, magazine follower down, then halfway in and rotate
steps.action: Line the bolt lugs up at 12 and 6 o'clock. The magazine follower has to be pressed down or the bolt will not enter. Slide the bolt about halfway into the receiver and rotate it until the bolt stop/guide clicks into its track, then push the handle down to lock it.
steps.aside:
NOTE: The magazine follower must be depressed to allow the bolt 
to enter the receiver.
steps.quote:
Slide the bolt assembly into the receiver approximately halfway
and rotate it until the bolt stop/guide clicks into its track.
steps.cite: McMillan TAC-50 Series Owner's Manual — McMillan-TAC-50-Series-Owners-Manual (the file McMillan publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — INSTALLATION OF THE BOLT ASSEMBLY

steps.title: Prove the firing pin falls — five times
steps.action: With the rifle empty and the trigger assembly clean: close the bolt, safety forward to FIRE, and pull the trigger. The firing pin must fall. Do it at least five times. ⛔ If the pin does not stay cocked when the bolt is closed smartly, the rifle goes back to McMillan — that is a sear that is not holding, on a .50.
steps.caution:
If the firing pin does not remain cocked, when the bolt 
is closed smartly, return the rifle to McMillan.
steps.quote:
The firing pin must
fall. Repeat at least 5 times.
steps.cite: McMillan TAC-50 Series Owner's Manual — McMillan-TAC-50-Series-Owners-Manual (the file McMillan publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — CLEANING THE RECEIVER AND TRIGGER ASSEMBLY

deepAbsentReason: McMillan publishes exactly one operation deeper than the guided clean above, and it is BOLT MAINTENANCE: with the bolt out, held with the handle towards you and the cocking piece up, the cocking piece housing is given an eighth of a turn clockwise to unlock the firing pin assembly from the bolt. That is where the published route ends. ⛔ Everything else is closed by name: the trigger "can be adjusted and maintained safely only by McMillan", a sticking ejector or extractor is a return-the-rifle condition rather than a repair, and a bore obstruction that will not push out with a rod goes back to the factory. So there is no deeper strip to present, and none has been borrowed from another .50.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Bore guide, coated rod, GOOD BRONZE brush — ⛔ never stainless
Chamber end towards the muzzle, always
Muzzle set LOWER than the action so solvent runs out, not in
Every 30–40 rounds with moly or copper-jacketed bullets

cleaning.name: BOLT
tasks: Solvent and a rag on the body until the fouling is gone
Bristle brush on the bolt face; loose brass off
Dry, then light oil; ejector and extractor worked to prove they move
A LIGHT film of grease behind the locking lugs — do not over-grease

cleaning.name: RECEIVER & TRIGGER
tasks: Stock off via the two action screws, rifle upside down
Cleaned as ONE unit with degreaser; degreaser off coated surfaces promptly
Light coat of oil, 15 minutes, then all excess wiped or blown off

cleaning.name: MUZZLE BRAKE
tasks: Checked for looseness every 50 rounds and tightened as necessary
⛔ The rifle is never fired without it

cleaning.name: ⛔ NEVER
tasks: WD-40, on any part of the rifle
A stainless brush in the bore
A trigger adjustment by anyone but McMillan

reassembly: Barrel confirmed free of obstructions and of patches before the bolt goes back.
Bolt lugs aligned at 12 and 6; magazine follower depressed.
Bolt in halfway, rotated until the bolt stop/guide clicks into its track, handle down.
Muzzle brake checked tight — and re-checked every 50 rounds thereafter.
Empty-chamber firing-pin test five times before the rifle is called ready.
fncheck: Rifle empty and reassembled: close the bolt, safety forward to FIRE, pull the trigger and feel the firing pin fall — five times over. Check the muzzle brake is tight; on a pinch-clamp brake the cross-bolt is 80–85 inch-pounds. ⛔ If the firing pin does not stay cocked when the bolt is closed smartly, stop and return the rifle to McMillan.
